issues.description: Tests fabricate a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash Addition sentinel to bypass the non-empty additions invariant
issues.detail: Test code switched from additions=[] to additions=[Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=zeros)] to satisfy CreateSignedTransaction's len>=1 check while real outputs come from extra_delta/cat_discrepancy. This is value-as-flag, weakens the postcondition that additions describe outputs, and signals the contract was bent to the code. Either relax the precondition or model absence honestly.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction complects three distinct request shapes into one record with unstated valid-field combinations
issues.detail: Adding extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution, and puzzle_decorator collapses XCH-send, CAT-spend, and signed-tx-creation into one type whose valid field combinations are not declared. Callers must know which subset is meaningful. Extract the transaction-building core as a function over a small CatDiscrepancy value object plus additions/fee/decorator, and let all handlers share it.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy invariant is duplicated across two dataclasses via a free validation function instead of a value type
issues.detail: The triple (extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution) is validated by membership-in-a-set with type: ignore and now lives in both CATSpend and CreateSignedTransaction. Lift it to a small CatDiscrepancy ADT constructed once at the boundary; the property becomes a plain field access, the ignores vanish, and the two classes stop being kept in sync by convention.

issues.description: send_transaction and cat_spend round-trip through json_serialize_for_transport to call a sibling in-process method
issues.detail: Building a typed CreateSignedTransaction, serializing it to JSON, then handing it to a sibling that deserializes it is transport-layer ceremony for an in-process call. This is framework where a library would do. Factor the shared core as a plain function over values and let both the RPC entry and the in-process callers invoke it directly.

issues.description: get_wallet called purely for its raising side effect with a '# opportunity to raise' comment hides intent
issues.detail: The discarded call communicates 'validate wallet of type X exists' through a comment instead of a name, and create_signed_transaction will redo the lookup. Introduce a validate_wallet_type(id, Wallet) helper that reads as validation, removing a line that future readers will be tempted to delete as dead code.

issues.description: puzzle_decorator typed as list but only the first element is consumed; comment admits it's a hack
issues.detail: The field is list[ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride] | None while a comment notes only Clawback is supported and only one entry is read. A list-of-one lies about its cardinality and bakes a leaky abstraction into a public request type. Make it ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride | None (or name it clawback_override) until the plural case actually exists.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the deduplication instinct is correct but the chosen shape is wrong: CreateSignedTransaction now complects three distinct request types into one record, callers synthesize a zero-amount sentinel Addition to satisfy its non-empty precondition, and in-process callers reach it via a JSON serialize/deserialize round trip. The cat_discrepancy triple is duplicated across two dataclasses and policed by a free function with type: ignores rather than captured as a small value object. Fix by extracting the transaction-building core as a plain function over a clean CatDiscrepancy ADT plus additions/fee/decorator, relaxing or honestly naming the additions precondition, and replacing the sentinel-addition test with one that exercises the real path. Smaller cleanups: name the wallet-type validation, and stop modeling puzzle_decorator as a list-of-one.
